metadata.title: ADVISOR: Autonomous Surface Ship for Guidance
metadata.description: EU ITEA Program — Escort-type Autonomous Surface Vehicle for cooperative navigation in constrained maritime environments.

AdvisorPage.title: ADVISOR: Autonomous Surface Ship for Guidance
AdvisorPage.subtitle: Escort-type autonomous surface vehicle, EU ITEA programme
AdvisorPage.overviewText: ADVISOR is an escort-type autonomous surface vehicle developed in the EU ITEA programme. It guides and escorts vessels in harbours and near-shore waters, with a human supervising.
AdvisorPage.fieldTrialText: Navigation, sensor fusion and decision-making are tested in real harbour conditions: convoy runs, obstacle avoidance and return to base.
AdvisorPage.fieldTrialCaption: Field trial setup in a harbour
AdvisorPage.fieldTrialImageAlt: Autonomous surface vehicle — Maritime Robotics platform for harbor and escort trials
AdvisorPage.navText: Seven sensor types are fused in real time for obstacle detection and path planning.
AdvisorPage.uwbDesc: Precise local positioning from fixed anchors
AdvisorPage.bathyText1: During operations the vessel also logs wind, air temperature, pressure and water depth for route planning and harbour surveys.
AdvisorPage.bathyCaption: Bathymetry and environmental data collection during field operations
AdvisorPage.bathyImageAlt: 3D bathymetric map on a display: color-coded seafloor depths with survey overlays during operations

metadata.title: Multi-Static Radar Systems
metadata.description: Spatially distributed radar for multi-target tracking and spatial diversity — IEEE RadarConf25 research by D7 Technology.

MultistaticPage.title: Multi-Static Radar Systems
MultistaticPage.subtitle: Distributed radar for multi-target tracking
MultistaticPage.overviewText: Multi-static radar places transmitters and receivers at different sites, so each target is seen from several angles. Small, low-RCS targets become easier to detect, and the system is less sensitive to clutter and interference.
MultistaticPage.simulationText: Plot-fusion algorithms are tested in Monte Carlo runs, measuring detection rate, false alarms and position error.
MultistaticPage.simulationCaption: Simulation map: radar nodes and target tracks
MultistaticPage.simulationImageAlt: Multi-panel simulation maps: atmospheric and polarimetric radar fields over west-east and south-north distance in kilometers
MultistaticPage.demoText: Plot fusion, track initiation and multi-target tracking in a simulated scenario.

WearableSensorsPage.title: Wearable Sensors & Performance Analysis
WearableSensorsPage.subtitle: UWB and IMU motion tracking and fall detection
WearableSensorsPage.overviewText: Wearable UWB and IMU sensors that track human motion, detect falls and measure athletic performance.
WearableSensorsPage.localizationText: UWB anchors on a calibrated indoor grid give sub-decimetre position accuracy, with synchronised IMU data for motion detail.
WearableSensorsPage.localizationImageAlt: Workstation display showing a precision localization and tracking interface used in controlled indoor tests
WearableSensorsPage.localizationCaption: Indoor test setup with UWB anchors
WearableSensorsPage.motionText: Machine learning on the fused UWB and IMU data classifies movement and separates falls from normal activity.
WearableSensorsPage.motionImageAlt: Abstract visualization representing large-scale motion and sensor-derived data for analysis pipelines
WearableSensorsPage.fieldText: Trials in sports and healthcare settings tested the system against multipath, body blocking and changing conditions.
WearableSensorsPage.fieldImageAlt: Athlete on an indoor court wearing ankle-mounted sensors during a motion capture style field experiment
WearableSensorsPage.uwbAnimCaption: UWB anchors take turns ranging to a tag; each range is a circle around its anchor.
WearableSensorsPage.imuAnimCaption: Accelerometer (ax, ay) and gyroscope (gz) traces, the raw input to the motion models.

metadata.title: Warehouse Automation & Order Picking
metadata.description: Reinforcement learning and swarm optimization for multi-agent order picking in steel warehouses — research and simulation platform by D7 Technology.

WarehouseAutomationPage.title: Warehouse Automation & Order Picking
WarehouseAutomationPage.subtitle: Reinforcement learning for multi-vehicle order picking
WarehouseAutomationPage.overviewText: Order picking is the slowest job in a warehouse. We route several picking vehicles through a steel warehouse so every order is collected in the shortest total time, without collisions in shared aisles.
WarehouseAutomationPage.approachText: A time-aware Ant Colony Optimization planner and deep reinforcement learning agents (DQN variants and PPO in PyTorch) run on the same layouts and orders, so they can be compared directly.
WarehouseAutomationPage.environmentText: Warehouses are JSON grid maps. The main layout models a real steel warehouse: a 30 × 28 grid with 289 product types.
WarehouseAutomationPage.platformText: A browser app runs experiments without code: upload a map, choose an algorithm, set training parameters and watch the run as video.
WarehouseAutomationPage.platformFigureAlt: Warehouse automation platform: map selection table and algorithm choice between ACO, RL and PPO
WarehouseAutomationPage.platformFigureCaption: Choosing a map and an algorithm
WarehouseAutomationPage.workflowFigureAlt: Operator panel listing uploaded warehouse maps with dimensions, product counts and status
WarehouseAutomationPage.workflowFigureCaption: Operator panel with uploaded warehouse maps
WarehouseAutomationPage.catalogFigureAlt: Product catalog view showing steel profile product codes with per-item order quantities
WarehouseAutomationPage.catalogFigureCaption: Building an order from the 289-product catalog
WarehouseAutomationPage.statusText: The ACO planner runs on full-size layouts and the RL agents train on the same environment. A public demo is in preparation.

metadata.title: Micro-Climate Forecasting: Rain & Wind
metadata.description: Live weather station data and rain and wind forecasts for the next 1, 6 and 24 hours — Single, Hybrid and Online models compared side by side, by D7 Technology.

MicroClimatePage.title: Micro-Climate Forecasting: Rain & Wind
MicroClimatePage.subtitle: Our own weather station and hourly rain and wind forecasts for the next 24 hours.
MicroClimatePage.overviewText: A weather station on our office window in Istanbul sends its readings to our server. Every hour, several models forecast wind and rain for this exact spot, and each forecast is later checked against what the station measured.
MicroClimatePage.issuesText: The station sits on a window: the building blocks the wind, the sun heats the temperature sensor, and the rain gauge has missed some rain. A mast and a radiation shield would fix most of this.

dashboard.nowCaption: Updated every minute. Wind reads low and temperature high because the sensors are next to the building.
dashboard.hourlyText: Line: wind. Dashed: gusts. Bars: chance of rain. Shows the Online blend unless you pick a model.
dashboard.hourlyCaption: Issued at {time} by {method}. Wind and gust in m/s; arrows show where the wind blows.
dashboard.successTitle: How often the forecasts are right
dashboard.successText: A forecast counts as right when wind is within 1 m/s, gusts within 2 m/s, or rain/no rain is called correctly. Target: 85–90 %. Green is on target, amber close, red below.
dashboard.successCaption: Last {days} days, {hours} hours checked; correct means within ±{tol} m/s. Grey rows are references: “No change” repeats the last hour, the weather services are their raw forecasts.
dashboard.successCaptionRain: Last {days} days, {hours} hours checked, {wet} of them wet. The rain gauge has missed some rain, so these scores are not reliable yet.
dashboard.verifyText: Coloured lines are forecasts, the black line is what the station measured.
dashboard.verifyNone: No checked forecasts in this period yet.
dashboard.verifyExample: For example, for {time} {method} forecast {pred} {unit}, {hours} h in advance; the station measured {obs} {unit}, a difference of {diff}.
dashboard.verifyCaption: Forecasts made {hours} h in advance, last 48 hours.
dashboard.compareText: Left of the dashed line is the past day's measurement, right of it the forecast.

status.needsWeek: starts after 7 days of station data
status.nextHour: first forecast at the next full hour

dashboard.historyCaption: Wind is the 10-minute mean, gust the strongest 3-second gust. Gaps mean no data.
dashboard.weightsTitle: How the Online blend weighs the models
dashboard.weightsText: Each model's share in the Online blend, based on its recent accuracy at each horizon.
dashboard.testedText: LightGBM tested on six months of nearby-station data it had not seen: how much smaller its error was than assuming no change.
dashboard.testedCaption: January to July 2026, 12–13 stations. Bars are cut at −60 %.

single.name: Single
single.text: LightGBM and SARIMA on the station's own data. Best for the next hour or two.

hybrid.name: Hybrid
hybrid.text: Start from the Open-Meteo forecast and learn how this spot differs. Best 6 to 24 hours ahead.

online.name: Online
online.text: A River model that learns every hour, and a blend that favours whichever model has been closest lately.

training.name: Training
training.text: LightGBM was pre-trained on 11 years of data from 13 nearby stations and is fine-tuned nightly on ours.

link.label: Data link
link.value: Signed readings over USB to a Raspberry Pi

server.label: Server
server.value: AWS with PostgreSQL, forecasts every hour

metadata.title: Indoor Positioning for Ship Model Tests
metadata.description: UWB, optical and inertial motion tracking for ship model tests in the YTU-MARINE pool, fused into a live digital twin. A D7 Technology project.

IndoorPositioningPage.title: Indoor Positioning for Ship Model Tests
IndoorPositioningPage.subtitle: UWB, optical and inertial tracking fused into a live digital twin
IndoorPositioningPage.overviewText: A motion-tracking system for ship model tests in the YTU-MARINE Research Center pool. Three independent sensing layers are fused into one estimate of the model's position and motion, for manoeuvring, seakeeping and autonomy tests.

uwb.name: UWB positioning
uwb.text: Nine anchors around the pool range to tags on the model about seven times a second.

optical.name: Optical tracking
optical.text: ArUco markers around the pool and a camera on the model.

inertial.name: Inertial and propulsion sensors
inertial.text: High-rate IMU data for linear and angular motion, plus propulsion readings.

IndoorPositioningPage.twinText: Every run appears live in a 3D model of the pool and is recorded, so any moment of a test can be replayed, not just the final results.
IndoorPositioningPage.twinCaption: The live digital twin during a run

Anim.caption: How our indoor positioning system tracks a model ship

Fusion.label: Indoor positioning
Fusion.heading: Three sensors. One track.
Fusion.text: UWB ranging, optical markers and inertial data are fused into one position estimate for every model ship run in the pool.

Hotspots.caption: The digital twin of the pool. Open a label to see what each part does.

ship.label: Model ship
ship.text: Carries the UWB tag, a camera, an IMU and propulsion sensors.

anchors.label: UWB anchors
anchors.text: Nine anchors around the pool range to the tag on the model about seven times a second.

markers.label: ArUco markers
markers.text: Printed markers in the pool give the onboard camera fixed points to measure against.

track.label: Fused track
track.text: One position estimate from all three sensors, drawn live and kept for replay.

sink.title: Sink
sink.text: The buoyancy engine draws oil into the hull, so the glider weighs slightly more than the water it displaces. The battery slides forward, the nose tips down and the wings turn the sinking into forward glide.

turn.title: Turn
turn.text: At the planned depth the pump pushes the oil out into an external bladder. The glider now displaces more water than it weighs and starts to rise.

climb.title: Climb
climb.text: The battery slides back, the nose tips up and the wings again turn vertical motion into forward travel, with no propeller running.

surface.title: Surface
surface.text: At the surface it gets a GPS fix, sends its data and takes new instructions, then dives again. The pump is the main energy cost, which is why gliders can stay at sea for weeks.
